extraction.identity_review: All four baseline identity layers were reviewed: 1,279 sites, 1,388 projects, both 231 identity-mapping records and 231 decisions, and 231 preserved source records. Atman, ATM S.A., WAW-2, Warsaw-2, Warszawa-2, Konstruktorska, CloudKleyer, Telehouse Poland and Thinx produced no candidate matches. The nearest existing host is Equinix WA2 at Poleczki 23, 3.581 km away, followed by WA4x at Krakowiaków 99, 4.186 km away. Both are distinct addresses and operators. WAW-1 at Grochowska 21A, WAW-3 in Duchnice and KTW-1 in Katowice are separate Atman hosts. One WAW-2 host and one existing-operation project are added; CloudKleyer equipment and the Thinx network node are not additional physical sites.

sources.title: Expedient: existing phoenixNAP Phoenix workloads retained following U.S. managed-cloud acquisition
sources.license: original publisher terms; compact factual projection only
sources.summary: Expedient's November 3 release says the acquired managed VMware and Veeam backup/disaster-recovery business is serving U.S. clients from phoenixNAP facilities in Phoenix and Ashburn. Clients retain their current environments, service levels, consoles and support engineers; movement to Expedient infrastructure is a future, client-agreed plan. This supports existing commercial operation of the separately identified Phoenix host on November 3, not a new opening or completion of an expansion. The acquisition concerns a services business and does not establish Expedient ownership or operation of the physical building.

extraction.date_semantics: November 3, 2026 is the visible original issuer dateline and URL date. Existing hosting is stated in the present tense; no retrieval or CMS modification date is used.
extraction.scope: Only the identified existing Phoenix host is admitted. Ashburn is mentioned but no second host is inferred here.
extraction.source_relationship: Original company-hosted release, independently corroborated by the same issuer-distributed PR Newswire release.
extraction.successor_review: The captured Expedient press index lists the November 5 Nutanix partnership announcement after the November 3 transaction. Its full article concerns cloud service capabilities and establishes no Phoenix physical relocation, closure or change of facility status. The original phoenixNAP scheduled-maintenance API records completed Phoenix cloud/Bare Metal maintenance through November 6 and separately future maintenance after retrieval; these service records corroborate continuity but do not identify a different host or prove commissioning of expansion. The RadiusDC press index contains the March acquisition announcement without a separately dated closing release. Current RadiusDC platform and county ownership identify the property, without supplying a closing date. No later primary physical closure or relocation was found in this bounded review through November 11. The November 3 release explicitly makes future workload migration client-agreed and prospective.

research_capture_indexes.research_scope: Phoenix identity, original dated hosting evidence and later-report review; unused Census candidate is retained as research only and supplies no selected coordinates.
